prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1297; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a reported rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports wrist pain and was transported to urgent care. Liability appears clear pending photo review of both vehicles.

Entry 2: Received notice that claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records for the right wrist. Diagnostic imaging shows a fracture of the distal radius. Treating orthopedist has recommended a splint and follow-up in several weeks.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the injury. Attorney indicates the claimant may require surgical consultation depending on healing. Requested itemized medical bills and wage documentation. Claimant is off work and employer has been asked to complete a wage verification form. Rental vehicle coverage confirmed under the policy.

Entry 4: Reviewed repair estimate for the insured vehicle and the third-party vehicle. Rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly damage noted on the claimant's vehicle. Supplement requested from shop for possible hidden frame damage. Photos uploaded to file. Attorney has been informed of the estimate review timeline.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's attorney on outstanding documents. Medical records received in part; remaining provider records requested again. Wage verification still pending from employer. Liability position remains under review with supervisor. Diary set to follow up in two weeks or upon receipt of records, whichever comes first.
